resultsCovered.label: Six months to 30 September 2026
sources: Interim reports to 31 Mar, 30 Jun and 30 Sep 2026 (unaudited)

price.note: 12-month range Rs 73.50–115.50. July–September 2026 Rs 84.00–97.70, closed September at Rs 84.50. Rights issue in May 2026 at Rs 72.

summary.headline: High returns, but growth has outrun its capital
summary.text: Vallibel Finance (VFIN.N0000) is a fast-growing finance company controlled by the Vallibel (Dhammika Perera) group, offering leasing, vehicle loans, gold loans and deposits. Its profits are strong (return on equity about 22%, group EPS Rs 8.96 in the six months to September 2026, up 21%), but the growth has been extreme: loans rose 70% in 2025/26 and another 9% by September, funded largely by borrowings that tripled. Capital is now thin even after a May 2026 rights issue at Rs 72: core capital 10.82% against a 10% minimum, total capital 14.75% against 14%. Non-performing loans doubled to Rs 7.5bn in a year, impairment charges rose sixfold, and no dividend was paid for 2025/26. At Rs 90.00 (CSE, 11 November 2026) it trades at 1.02x NAV (Rs 88.25) and 5.4x trailing earnings. Three methods put fair value at about Rs 80, so the price is about 13% above it. I'd buy at up to Rs 67.90 and treat under Rs 59.90 as a strong buy.

quality.reason: High returns and steady profits, but capital is barely above the minimum and no dividend was paid for 2025/26.

tests.label: Return on equity of 15% or more
Capital comfortably above the minimum (finance company)
tests.note: Minimum 10%; total capital 14.75% (minimum 14%). Down from 16.5% and 21.5% in March 2025 despite a Rs 2.1bn rights issue.

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: EPS halved in 2022/23 (Rs 5.69 from Rs 12.37) but no loss.

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends
tests.note: Rs 2.75 for 2024/25; profit is being retained (and new capital raised) to fund loan growth. Interest cover only 1.5x.

valuation.note: Fair value weights the bear/base/bull averages of three methods 30/50/20 (about 0.91x NAV). The dividend model isn't used because no dividend was paid for 2025/26.

highlights.title: Six months to September 2026 (unaudited)
highlights.text: Group profit up 31% to Rs 2.35bn (EPS Rs 8.96 against Rs 7.41). Net interest income up 44% to Rs 7.24bn; impairment charges Rs 886m against Rs 140m. ROE 21.8%.

highlights.title: Bad loans doubling
highlights.text: Gross non-performing loans rose to Rs 7.53bn from Rs 3.52bn a year earlier (about 4.4% of loans, from 2.5% in March). Net NPLs Rs 2.16bn against a net negative a year ago.

highlights.title: Thin capital despite a rights issue
highlights.text: A 1-for-8 rights issue at Rs 72 raised Rs 2.12bn in May 2026, but core capital is only 10.82% (minimum 10%) and total capital 14.75% (minimum 14%), because loans keep growing (Rs 171bn, up 9% in six months).

highlights.title: 2025/26 (audited)
highlights.text: EPS Rs 15.12 (group), ROE about 20–22%. Lending up 70% to Rs 156.5bn, borrowings up from Rs 21bn to Rs 70bn. No dividend (Rs 2.75 the year before).

methodReadings.reading: High, but partly from very high leverage (debt and deposits about 8x equity).
Trailing group EPS Rs 16.67; year-end P/E 3.0–6.2x over five years.
Profit is retained to fund growth; a dividend model would give only Rs 12–36, so it isn't used.
Barely above the 10% minimum; more capital raising (and dilution) is likely if growth continues.
Doubled in a year as the 2025 loan book seasons; impairments up sixfold.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: Book value Rs 88.25 × (ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth): ROE 14% / 17% / 20%.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: ROE moving from 21.8% to 14% / 17% / 20% over ten years; 20% payout.

modelsNote: A finance company, so residual income and justified price-to-book replace a DCF, alongside P/E. I use a higher cost of equity (19% base) than for the banks because capital is thin, leverage high and bad loans rising.

scenarios.common: 10-year government bond about 12.4% plus about 6.5 points for a highly leveraged finance company with thin capital. Base EPS assumes the second half is similar to the first, with impairments still elevated.

sensitivity.title: Residual income base case, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Today's Rs 90 needs a long-run ROE of about 18% at a 19% cost of equity.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 35,150 in total, against Rs 45,000 at Rs 90.00.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 67.90 is below the 12-month low of Rs 73.50 and the Rs 72 rights price, so it needs a market fall or bad news on loans.

higher: Capital rebuilt to 13%+ core without heavy dilution.
NPLs stabilising below 4% with ROE above 20%.
lower: Another rights issue at a low price.
Capital ratios breaching the minimum, forcing slower growth.
Higher funding costs (interest cover is only 1.5x).

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2024/25 and 2025/26 annual reports and the interim reports to September 2026 (unaudited). This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

Decision box.Verdict: Overpriced: about 13% above fair value of Rs 80.
Decision box.Expected yearly return at Rs 90: About 11% a year: no dividend + book growth about 15% − about 4% a year if the price moved to fair value, with high risk.
Decision box.Confidence: Low to medium: profits are strong, but capital is thin and bad loans are rising fast.
Decision box.Margin of safety: Buy 15% below fair value (Rs 67.90), strong buy 25% below (Rs 59.90).

Business and moat.What it does: Leasing, vehicle loans, gold loans and other lending, funded by deposits and bank borrowings; a subsidiary holds property.
Business and moat.Moat: Narrow: part of the Vallibel group, with a growing branch network; competes with banks and larger finance companies.

Management and governance.Ownership: Vallibel Investments (Pvt) Ltd 51.4% and K.A.D.D. (Dhammika) Perera 21.4%; the Perera family about 7% more. Public float small.

Sri Lanka checks.Interest rates: Risk: interest cover 1.5x; funding is mostly deposits and bank borrowings.
Sri Lanka checks.Credit cycle: Risk: loans grew 70% in a year; NPLs are rising.
Sri Lanka checks.Regulation: Capital barely above Central Bank minimums.

Investment case and sell rules.Why own it: High-ROE lender, only at a discount to NAV.
Investment case and sell rules.Sell triggers: Price above Rs 103.90 (30% above fair value); core capital below the minimum; NPLs above 6%.

What this analysis doesn't cover: Loan mix by product (gold, vehicle, SME) and where the NPLs are.
